The present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal procedure, 19731 seeks quashing of Criminal Complaint No. 71/96 filed under Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954,2 as well as order dated 25th May, 2012, rejecting the Petitioners' applications for discharge in this complaint.
2.

The aforenoted complaint has been instituted against the Petitioners for alleged violation of Section 2(ix)(k) of the PFA Act read with Rules 32(e) and 50(7) of the PFA Rules, 1955, which is stated to constitute an offence punishable under Section 16(1) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act.

It is further alleged in the complaint that the Petitioners imported misbranded food articles in contravention of Section 5 of the PFA Act.

sentences.text: Mr. Pramod Kumar Dubey, Senior Counsel for the Petitioners, submits that even if the prosecution's case is taken at its highest, the allegations against the Petitioners pertain solely to misbranding and not adulteration.

In this regard, he places reliance on the Public Analyst's report dated 4th November, 1995, which records that the sample was misbranded owing to violation of Rule 32(e) and (f) of the PFA Rules, 1955, and contains no finding whatsoever of adulteration.

He contends that a first-time allegation of misbranding does not warrant criminal prosecution in view of the Government of India's policy dated 23rd September, 1985, which mandates issuance of only a warning for a first offence.

He submits that this policy has been recognised by this Court in multiple decisions, including Hindustan Unilever v. State (NCT of Delhi) & Ors.,3 which in turn relied upon the earlier decision in S.S. Gokal Krishnan & Ors. v. NCT of Delhi.4

sentences.text: On this basis alone, he contends that the impugned complaint deserves to be quashed.

4. Mr. Dubey further submits that the status report filed by the State is entirely misconceived in alleging violation of Rule 50(7) of the PFA Rules, which reads as under:
"Rule 50: Conditions for Licence:-
..xx.. ..xx.. ..xx..
(7) Proprietors of [hotels, restaurants and other food stalls (including mobile and itinerant food stalls who sell or expose for sale savouries, sweets or other articles of food) shall put up a notice board containing "PFA Act"
2011 [1] JCC 689.
2009 CRI. L.J. 1386.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 06/12/2025 at 20:36:03 separate lists of the articles which have been cooked in ghee, edible oil, [vanaspati] and other fats for the information of the intending purchasers.]"
5. He submits that Rule 50(7) applies only to proprietors of hotels, restaurants and food stalls, and has no application to food vendors.
Therefore, the alleged violation is wholly misconceived, and the complaint, in his submission, deserves to be set aside on this ground as well.

6. List for further submissions on 16th December, 2025.
SANJEEV NARULA, J DECEMBER 6, 2025/as
